common_name: Casa Blanca Oriental Lily (Giant Pure White Fragrant Cut-Flower Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall (November–December) in zone 9 for late spring to early summer bloom; orient bulbs pointed end up, 5–6 inches deep, and give afternoon shade where summer sun is intense. In zone 9's warm winters, lift and refrigerate bulbs for about 8 weeks at 34–40°F before fall replanting to sustain vigorous bloom in future years.

directions: Plant bulbs 5–6 inches deep in fall with the pointed end up, and mulch over the planting area to moderate soil temperature and conserve moisture. Casa Blanca is one of the most widely grown Oriental hybrid lilies in the world, producing enormous, pure white, outward-facing flowers 8–10 inches across with gently recurved petals and prominent rust-orange anthers, held on tall, sturdy stems that make it a favorite for both garden borders and cut-flower arrangements. Its intense, sweet fragrance is among the strongest of any lily, capable of scenting an entire room or garden area from a single planting, and the flawless white blooms pair elegantly with almost any color scheme. Stake taller stems in windy sites to protect the heavy flower heads, and remove spent blooms before they set seed to redirect energy back into the bulb for next year's display.
